Reallocate only within A-O under a signed map. If M fails, remap D-101H to clear STOCK-A before purchasing panel stock. Use finished-white-oak N/O only for a documented short-member fallback; do not crosscut a long critical board to solve a short-part shortage.
Prove the whole-thickness staged plane/rest/carrier method on representative coupons, then prove STOCK-B and STOCK-C at full length.
B yields the D-101A show face and C yields the D-101B show face, each continuous and glue-ready at 5/16 x 4-3/8 x 81-1/8 with no taper, end joint, defect, or unstable grain.
Stop and obtain replacement continuous face stock. Do not shorten, end-splice, or veneer over a failed stile face.
Prove the two full-length stile lanes in STOCK-I and STOCK-K before making the single width rip.

Each board has at least 8-7/8 inches of clear jointed width for two 4-3/8-inch lanes plus the 1/8-inch kerf; each yields one straight 7/8 x 4-3/8 x 81 core and one continuous 5/16 x 4-3/8 x 81-1/8 back face after staged planing and rest. K retains the hinge and screw zones; I retains the lock envelope.
Stop and purchase only a replacement long layer for the failed stile. Reducing the 4-1/4-inch finished stile or joining any long layer end-to-end is not authorized.
Create and sign the revised CM-05 before cutting J or L. Because L is now 6 inches wide, J carries C, M, the 6-1/2-inch F stave, and G; L carries E, both D staves, and the 5-3/4-inch F stave.

J yields three 16-1/4-inch core mother billets for C, M, and the 6-1/2-inch F stave plus one 12-inch G billet; J must retain at least one clear 6-1/2-inch jointed width envelope. Every core is 7/8 inch, clear, continuous in length, and traceable; usable width offcuts are retained for FP-05, whose source pool also requires at least five clear 16-1/4-inch mother billets combined from E/F.

Rearrange only clear J/L envelopes under a revised signed map. If the core map fails, prefer a clear finished-white-oak STOCK-N or STOCK-O short-core remap; if that also fails, purchase only the failed core stock. Never consume a critical stile layer.

Complete and sign FP-05 using up to two clear 16-1/4-inch STOCK-M tail billets after D-101H passes, plus D/H tails, eligible C/J/L longitudinal offcuts, and the required remaining clear mother billets from knot-mapped E/F. Keep STOCK-A intact unless a signed substitution is required.

Reassign clear pool strips without moving a released seam. Keep N/O out of the face pool unless a signed remap accepts the excessive thickness-planing loss. If the complete A-O pool still fails, purchase only the missing face billet; do not alter a stile layer or core allocation.

Only after CHK-RS-01, CHK-ST-01, and CHK-ST-02 pass, verify thickness and warp throughout every mapped M/G/H/D clear envelope. If M fails, remap D-101H to clear STOCK-A. Use clear E/F or uncommitted J/L only after the structural short-member map passes; otherwise purchase replacement panel stock.

Press and destructively inspect same-layup coupons before every structural member family; coupon face stock must use the same whole-thickness staged plane/rest/carrier preparation as its production family.

The 5/16 + 7/8 + 5/16 layup measures 1-1/2 before surfacing, cures without voids or slip, then finishes 1/4 + 7/8 + 1/4 at 1-3/8. Sectioned groove and DF samples retain at least 0.200 actual core wood to each face glue line and fail in wood rather than at the adhesive line.
Correct moisture, surface preparation, adhesive spread, pressure, platen, or cauls and remake the coupon. Production members remain on hold.
Transfer and verify the D-101D and D-101F three-plane seam maps after final width but before Domino machining.

D core/show/back seams are 2-1/4, 4-3/8, and 4-7/8 from top. F core seam is 5-3/4; show seams are 3, 6-1/2, and 9-1/2; back seams are 2-1/2, 5, and 9. Rebuild the affected sheet or core. Do not move a Domino center without revising the specification, register, story stick, templates, drawings, and lock gate.
Each board is confirmed finished white oak at 1-3/4 x 11 x 74 inches and equals 9.90 board feet. At 74 inches neither board can replace an 81-inch continuous stile layer.

A's original 78-3/4-inch length is obsolete; six inches are charged to damage removal. M is newly reported as finished white oak and now carries D-101H plus up to two conditional face-pool billets.

Keep A intact as reserve. Verify M's actual finished dimensions, straightness, moisture, grain, and clear envelope; cut three 16-1/16-inch M panel billets only after CHK-RS-01/CHK-ST-01/CHK-ST-02 pass.
The original 7-inch width is obsolete. The current 6-inch edge-cleaned width cannot yield the planned 6-1/2-inch F core stave.
